classification.difficultyReason: Combine input and output translations to sketch the supplied logarithmic curve, keeping its vertical asymptote and representative points consistent with the shifts.

content.prompt: Sketch the following graphs by applying a translation to $y=\ln x$. The original curve is given.

spec.description: Unscaled Cartesian axes with the original logarithmic curve only; no ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Original curve y=ln x, parametrised by (exp(t),t); vertical asymptotic behaviour at x=0.
spec.answerVisibility: Original curve always visible; transformed curve excluded.

answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $x-1$ translates the graph 1 unit right. Each point $(x,y)$ moves to $(x+1,y)$. The vertical asymptote moves to $x=1$.

spec.description: Original logarithmic curve compared with the same curve translated 1 unit right; both have downward and rightward continuation arrows.
spec.mathematics: Original (exp(t),t); image (exp(t)+1,t). No numerical scale or extra dashed asymptote.

spec.description: Unscaled Cartesian axes and original logarithmic curve, without solution curve or dashed asymptote.
spec.mathematics: y=ln x; no numerical scale or grid.

answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $x+2$ translates the graph 2 units left. Each point $(x,y)$ moves to $(x-2,y)$. The vertical asymptote moves to $x=-2$.

spec.description: Original curve and heavier transformed curve 2 units left, with a dashed vertical asymptote left of the y-axis.
Unscaled Cartesian axes and original logarithmic curve only.
spec.mathematics: y=ln x; vertical asymptotic behaviour at x=0; no ticks or grid.

answer.short: Translate 1 unit left and 2 units up.
answer.worked: Write $y-2=\ln(x+1)$. Replacing $x$ with $x+1$ and $y$ with $y-2$ translates the graph 1 unit left and 2 units up. Each point $(x,y)$ moves to $(x-1,y+2)$. The vertical asymptote is $x=-1$, and the graph passes through $(0,2)$.

spec.description: Original curve compared with a heavier curve translated left and up; dashed asymptote left of the y-axis and continuation arrows.
spec.mathematics: Image (exp(t)-1,t+2); asymptote x=-1. The lower parameter range is extended to retain the downward continuation within the same frame.
